points.description: States an effect on Paul: learning Mr. Leonard's background (he was a champion hurdler who struggled with reading/school, lost his scholarship and flunked out) makes Paul relate to/empathize with him, since Paul recognizes the same feelings of embarrassment and struggle. Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the effect is stated vaguely (e.g. 'Paul understands Mr. Leonard better') without saying he relates to or identifies with the shared struggles.

points.description: Supports with a relevant detail from the story, e.g. Paul realizes he can help Mr. Leonard and invites him to start his own training ('It's time to start your training'), or the emotions in Mr. Leonard's words were 'all too familiar' to Paul, or Paul's own embarrassment about reading aloud. The detail must be linked to the effect.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if a detail is accurate but not clearly connected to the effect on Paul.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a clear effect on Paul (empathy/connection, motivation to help Mr. Leonard) plus a linked story detail. Part marks for an effect with no or weakly linked support, or a detail with a vague effect. No marks for plot summary with no effect on Paul or for inaccurate claims.
rubric.answer_key: Learning Mr. Leonard's past as a record-setting hurdler who lost his scholarship because he couldn't handle the reading and schoolwork makes Paul see they share the same struggles and feelings ("The emotions... were all too familiar to me"). This inspires Paul to want to repay Mr. Leonard's help, so he invites him to begin his own training ("It's time to start your training").
